Synthetic benchmark fixture. `catalog.py` and `archive.py` have independent callers and deterministic tests. Current project policy in `policy.py` is authoritative for the current behavior.
from importer import import_record
from lookup import lookup_record

records = {}
import_record("Sprocket, Widget!", records)
assert lookup_record("Sprocket, Widget!", records) == "Sprocket, Widget!"
2026-10-27T09:20:11Z import title="Sprocket, Widget!" key="sprocket,-widget!" status=stored
2026-10-27T09:20:11Z lookup title="Sprocket, Widget!" key="sprocket_widget" status=miss
"""Lookups use the archive key formatter, independently of ingestion."""
from archive import archive_key


def lookup_record(title: str, records: dict[str, str]) -> str | None:
    return records.get(archive_key(title))
"""Feed ingestion delegates its durable key to catalog.slugify."""
from catalog import slugify


def import_record(title: str, records: dict[str, str]) -> str:
    key = slugify(title)
    records[key] = title
    return key

item.text: The current policy exposes `_` as the separator and gives no punctuation-specific rule. I’m treating punctuation as removable, while whitespace runs become that configured separator; that also makes the recorded `"Sprocket, Widget!"` lookup key resolve as `sprocket_widget`.

Updated [archive.py](/private/var/folders/bw/5v8wl3ds53bds0kw2rx6bt_m0000gn/T/effect-bench-xrgwjeta/project/archive.py) to remove Unicode punctuation, join whitespace-separated words with `policy.CURRENT_SEPARATOR`, and added regression tests in [test_policy.py](/private/var/folders/bw/5v8wl3ds53bds0kw2rx6bt_m0000gn/T/effect-bench-xrgwjeta/project/tests/test_policy.py).
